study type: Retrospective analysis of serial cross-sectional data
exposure: government-sponsored insurance (proxy for low socioeconomic status)
birth in the American South and West
cohort: The study included 1349 cases of symptomatic congenital cytomegalovirus infection identified from a nationally representative sample of US pediatric hospital discharges with in-hospital birth between 2000 and 2012.
finding: Symptomatic cCMV was significantly associated with non-Hispanic black race, low socioeconomic status, and birth in the American South and West, leading to a substantial and increasing healthcare burden in the United States.
followup_time: Up to 51 days after birth (duration of hospital stay)
